rows.description: I love when my grandmother tells old stories while oiling my hair. Warmth and belonging come from these moments. I listen, ask questions and remember. Time with her is a gift.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger
related mind states: affection, nostalgia

rows.description: My grandfather repeats the same advice and I roll my eyes. Some of it feels old-fashioned. I can listen patiently and still make my own choices. Rude answers cost more than they seem.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection
related mind states: anger

rows.description: My grandmother spoils me with sweets and lets me skip chores. It feels lovely but my parents set rules. I enjoy it without using her against my parents. Wise kids know both kinds of love.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: affection, anger
related mind states: affection

rows.description: My friend promised to come to my birthday and did not show. I am hurt. I tell her calmly what it felt like and ask why. Snapping back or refusing to talk leaves the hurt untouched.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: distrust, forgiveness, shame
related mind states: disappointment, calm, hurt

rows.description: She said sorry and explained. I forgive her, though I may be careful for a while. Forgiveness means letting go of anger, not pretending nothing happened. If it keeps happening, I say so.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, distrust, shame
related mind states: anger

rows.description: I broke my promise to my friend and I am too embarrassed to face her. Hiding worsens things. Wise: tell her the truth, say sorry, and try to make it up. Honest apologies heal.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, distrust, forgiveness
related mind states: shame, embarrassment

rows.description: After being let down again and again, I stop believing her promises. Protecting myself is fine. I can still be friendly and stop counting on her for big things. Not cruel, only careful.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: disillusionment, forgiveness, shame
related mind states: disappointment

rows.subtopic: Blamed for something I did not do
rows.description: I was blamed for something I did not do and I feel hot with unfairness. I explain calmly with facts and ask for a fair look. Shouting or crying is understandable but less effective. A parent can help.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, fear
related mind states: sadness, calm

rows.subtopic: Blamed for something I did not do
rows.description: A friend let me take the blame to save herself. I feel deeply betrayed. I can tell her I saw what she did and hear her out. Trust breaks, and I decide slowly whether to repair it.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fairness, fear
related mind states: trust

rows.subtopic: Blamed for something I did not do
rows.description: I let my friend take the blame because I was scared. Afterward I feel sick. The brave step is to go to the teacher and admit the truth, then apologise to her. Fear passes; regret stays.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, fairness
related mind states: fear, regret
